Aman reads Android’s per-app network usage totals locally to look for unusual background upload combined with risky control or spyware signals. It does not read packet contents, photos, messages, passwords or HTTPS data, and it does not upload the statistics. Android Usage Access must be granted manually. The normal background check uses one lightweight total-upload counter and only runs the more expensive per-app query after a meaningful upload burst or about every 6 hours.

This verifies automatic external-link interception, not just the scanner. Aman must hold Android’s browser role. The test launches AMTSO as a normal system web link; Android should route it into Aman, where the exact harmless phishing-test URL is stopped. The DNS shield cannot see an encrypted HTTPS path, so typing or navigating to this test from inside another browser is outside this URL-level test.
